Build the between-response covariance and its derivatives under a graph

Source: R/between_graph.R
mc_build_sigma_between_graph.Rd

Maps a vector of graph parameters to the between-response covariance \(\Sigma_b\) and to the list of its derivatives with respect to each parameter, in the list form consumed by the estimating-function engine of mcglm_graph. It takes the place that the correlation-based between-response builder has in a multivariate covariance generalized linear model (MCGLM). For the Gaussian graphical model (GGM) layer, \(\Sigma_b = (\sum_d \eta_d Z_d)^{-1}\) and \(\partial\Sigma_b/\partial\eta_d = -\Sigma_b Z_d \Sigma_b\); for the directed acyclic graph (DAG) layer, \(\Sigma_b = T^{-1} D T^{-\top}\), with \(T = I - \Gamma\) and \(D = \mathrm{diag}(\delta)\), and the derivatives are taken with respect to \(\gamma\) and \(\delta\), the innovation variances themselves and not their logarithms. Matrices are returned in the order of the responses, whatever the DAG ordering.

Usage

mc_build_sigma_between_graph(theta_G, n_resp, spec, inverse = FALSE)

Arguments

theta_G

numeric vector of graph parameters. For "ggm": the \(\eta\) vector (diagonal parameters, then edges in canonical order, length \(R + |E|\)). For "dag": c(gamma, delta), with the \(|E|\) coefficients \(\gamma\), one per edge, sorted lexicographically by the positions of its endpoints in the ordering (the canonical edge order under the natural ordering), followed by the \(R\) innovation variances \(\delta\), indexed by position in the ordering. The GGM vector must give a positive-definite precision, otherwise an error is raised; the DAG vector is expected to have \(\delta > 0\), which is not checked.

n_resp

integer, number of responses \(R\).

spec

an object of class "mcg_graph_spec" from mc_between_graph.

inverse

logical; if TRUE, also return the precision matrix.

Value

A list with Sigmab (the \(R \times R\) covariance), D_Sigmab (list of derivatives, one per element of theta_G), edge_pos (positions of the edge parameters in theta_G) and, when inverse = TRUE, Kb (the precision matrix).

See also

mc_between_graph, mc_precision_bases

Examples

sp <- mc_between_graph("ggm")
out <- mc_build_sigma_between_graph(c(2, 2, 2, -0.4, -0.3, 0), 3, sp)
out$Sigmab
#>           [,1]      [,2]  [,3]
#> [1,] 0.5333333 0.1066667 0.080
#> [2,] 0.1066667 0.5213333 0.016
#> [3,] 0.0800000 0.0160000 0.512
